text: The fan in my room in Hostel A has been intermittent since last week; it stops randomly during the night, making it impossible to sleep in this heat.
All the sockets in the common room of South Block are dead, so we can't charge our laptops while studying together for the finals.
The light in the corridor on the third floor of Hostel B flickers constantly, which is really distracting when I'm trying to review my syllabus late at night.
During the peak afternoon heat, the power went out for three hours, and with no fan, my room felt like an oven—I couldn't even nap before my 2 PM class.
The socket near my desk suddenly sparked and now doesn't work, so I have to charge my phone across the room, which is inconvenient during online lectures.
The fan in my roommate's side of the room works fine, but mine has been making a grinding noise for days, and maintenance hasn't come despite multiple requests.
Every evening around 7 PM, the lights in the hostel mess dim significantly, making it hard to see what we're eating, and the food already isn't great.
The power outage last night caused my router to reset, and I lost all my unsaved assignment work right before the deadline.
In Hostel C, the sockets in the study area are so loose that chargers keep falling out, interrupting device charging during crucial study sessions.
The fan speed regulator in my room is faulty; it only works on the highest setting, which is too noisy for sleeping.
During the mid-term exams, the lights in my room suddenly went out, and I had to finish revising by candlelight—totally unacceptable.
The electrical socket in the bathroom doesn't work, so I can't use my electric shaver, and I have to go to a friend's room every morning.
The power supply in East Block is so unstable that my desk lamp keeps flickering, giving me headaches during late-night study marathons.
Last Tuesday, the fan in my room stopped working entirely, and with the temperatures soaring, I've had to sleep in the common room for two nights.
The sockets near the windows in Hostel D are exposed to rain during storms, and they short-circuited, causing a minor scare—we need weatherproofing.
The hallway lights on the ground floor of Hostel A are out, making it dangerous to walk at night, especially after late library sessions.
My fan's remote control doesn't work, and the wall switch is across the room, so I have to get up every time to adjust it—very frustrating during sleep.
The power went out just as I was about to submit my online exam, and by the time it came back, the submission portal had closed.
In the hostel kitchenette, the socket for the microwave is faulty, so we can't heat our mess food when it's cold, which is often.
The fan in my room makes a constant humming sound that gets louder at night, disturbing my sleep before early morning classes.
The lights in the staircase from the first to second floor in Hostel B have been out for a week, and several students have almost tripped in the dark.
During the group project meeting in my room, all the sockets suddenly lost power, so we couldn't charge our laptops and had to cut the session short.
The fan in the common area of Hostel C is so slow it doesn't circulate air, making study groups unbearable during hot afternoons.
The electrical outlet in my room sparked and emitted a burning smell, so I unplugged everything, but maintenance hasn't checked it yet—safety hazard!
Every time it rains, the power in Hostel D flickers, and once it went out for hours, ruining my frozen snacks in the mini-fridge.
The desk lamp I bought for studying short-circuited due to voltage fluctuations in the hostel, and now I'm left without proper lighting.
The fan in my room only works when it wants to; sometimes it starts, sometimes it doesn't, and it's driving me crazy during this heatwave.
The sockets in the hostel gym are all non-functional, so we can't charge our phones or use audio devices while working out.
The light in my closet burnt out, and I can't see my clothes in the morning, making me late for my 8 AM lectures.
During the final exam week, the power was cut for maintenance without prior notice, disrupting my all-night study plan.
The fan speed is so low that it feels like a gentle breeze, not enough to cool the room, especially after coming back from sports practice.
The electrical panel in Hostel A makes a buzzing sound constantly, and we're worried it might lead to a bigger issue if not fixed.
The socket behind my bed is loose, and my phone charger keeps disconnecting, causing my alarm to not charge and making me oversleep.
The lights in the hostel library are too dim in some sections, and with sockets not working, we can't even use our own lamps.
The fan in my room has a broken blade, so it wobbles noisily and I'm afraid it might fall off—need immediate replacement.
Power surges have damaged my laptop charger twice now, and the hostel administration hasn't done anything about stabilizing the voltage.
The hallway lights on the fourth floor of Hostel B turn off automatically after 10 PM, but students are still studying, so it's pitch dark.
The socket in my room only provides power intermittently; my phone charges for a few minutes then stops, and it's frustrating during important calls.
During the hostel festival preparations, the lights in the common hall kept tripping, delaying our decoration work.
The fan in the computer lab of the hostel is out of order, making the room stuffy and uncomfortable for long coding sessions.
The light switch in my bathroom is faulty; sometimes it turns on, sometimes it doesn't, and I've had to shower in the dark a few times.
The power outage during dinner time meant the mess food was served cold, and with no way to heat it, we had to eat as is.
The sockets in the hostel TV room are all occupied or broken, so we can't plug in our gaming consoles for weekend relaxation.
The fan in my room is covered in dust and makes a wheezing sound, but when I asked for cleaning, they said it's an electrical issue.
The lights in the hostel courtyard don't work, making it unsafe for evening walks or late-night returns from the lab.
The electrical wiring in Hostel C is exposed in some places, and with the rains, it's a serious risk of electrocution.
My table fan stopped working right before my exams, and with the room fan also faulty, I had to study in the common area which is always noisy.
The power cut during the online lecture caused me to miss important notes, and the recording wasn't available, so I'm behind on syllabus.
The sockets in the hostel laundry room are not working, so we can't use the washing machines, and clothes are piling up.
The fan in my room has a short circuit; it turns on by itself sometimes in the middle of the night, scaring me awake.
The lights in the hostel staircase are motion-activated but they take too long to turn on, causing near misses on the steps.
During the heatwave, the hostel administration reduced fan speed to save power, but it's making sleep impossible during hot nights.
The socket for my refrigerator tripped the circuit breaker, and now I lost all my perishable food for the week.
The fan in the study room of Hostel D is so loud it distracts from concentration, but without it, the room is too hot.
The power supply in the hostel is erratic during peak hours, affecting my online lab simulations which require stable internet.
The light in my room flickers every time I turn on the fan, which is annoying when I'm trying to read before bed.
The sockets in the hostel corridors are meant for vacuum cleaners but they don't work, so cleaning is hampered.
The fan remote in my room needs new batteries, but the electrical shop on campus is always out of stock, and the wall switch is broken.
The lights in the hostel garden are out, making it difficult for security patrols and students returning late from library.
The power outage during my online certification exam caused me to be disqualified, and I have to retake it next month.
The dal served in the mess every day is so watery and tasteless; it's like drinking seasoned water instead of a proper lentil soup.
I found a piece of plastic in my rice during dinner last night, and this is the third time this month! How is this acceptable?
The mess staff consistently runs out of chapatis by 8 PM, leaving those of us from late classes with only cold rice and leftovers.
For the past week, the vegetables in the curry have been so overcooked that they're mushy and completely unappetizing.
The food in Block C mess is always cold by the time we get it, especially during the 7 PM dinner shift. Can't you keep it warm?
I paid for the mess plan expecting decent meals, but the quality has dropped so much that I'm considering eating outside, which is expensive.
There's no variety in the breakfast menu—it's always idli or poha, and both are so bland they need tons of salt to be edible.
During exam season, when we need nutritious food, the mess serves the same oily and greasy dishes that make it hard to focus.
The rotis are often hard and chewy, as if they were made hours ago and just reheated. Fresh ones would be much better.
I suspect the oil used in cooking is reused too many times; the food has a strange aftertaste and gives me stomach aches.
Why is there never enough salad? The few pieces of cucumber and tomato are usually wilted and unfresh.
The mess hall in Hostel 12 is so crowded during lunch that by the time I get my food, it's cold and unappetizing.
The sambhar served today had a sour taste, like it was fermented for too long. This is a health hazard!
We were promised a special dinner on weekends, but it's just the usual fare with a dessert that's often too sweet or stale.
I'm a vegetarian, and twice this week, the vegetable dish had traces of meat in it. This is completely unacceptable and disrespectful.
The mess fees were increased last semester, but the food quality has only worsened. Where is the money going?
The serving spoons are often dirty or sticky, which makes me question the overall hygiene standards of the mess.
For the 9 AM breakfast, the milk is sometimes lukewarm instead of hot, and the cornflakes are soggy.
The chicken curry on Sunday was so bony with hardly any meat; it felt like we were just paying for bones and gravy.
During my late-night study sessions, I wish the mess kept some snacks available, but everything is closed by 10 PM.
The rice is always undercooked or overcooked—never just right. It's either too hard or mushy.
The mess menu is posted but rarely followed. We expect one thing and get another, which is frustrating.
The food portions for girls are sometimes smaller, assuming we eat less, but that's not fair; we pay the same fees.
The dining area smells of stale food because the cleaning isn't done properly after meals. It's off-putting.
I wrote a complaint about the mess food last week, but nothing has changed. Is anyone even reading these?
The paneer dish served yesterday was so rubbery and tasteless, it was like eating erasers. Can't you cook it properly?
In Hostel Block B, the mess starts closing at 8:30 PM sharp, even if students are still coming from labs. Can we extend the time?
The fruit provided is often unripe or overripe—bananas are either green or black, never just yellow.
The eggs in the breakfast buffet are sometimes undercooked, with runny yolks that might not be safe to eat.
There's no option for low-spice food for those who can't handle heat; everything is loaded with chilies.
The mess staff is rude when we ask for extra portions or complain about the food. Some courtesy would be nice.
The water dispenser in the mess is often empty, and we have to go elsewhere to get drinking water.
The food served during festival days is supposed to be special, but last Diwali, the sweets were store-bought and stale.
I've seen insects flying around the food counter in the evening. Please install mosquito nets or improve pest control.
The bread for toast is often stale, and when toasted, it becomes so hard it's difficult to chew.
The mess committee meetings are held, but student feedback never seems to impact the actual food quality.
The curry is so oily that there's a layer of grease on top, which is unhealthy and unappetizing.
For students with allergies, there's no labeling of ingredients. I'm allergic to peanuts, and I'm always worried.
The mess menu repeats every two weeks exactly, making meals monotonous and boring.
The food temperature is inconsistent—sometimes piping hot, sometimes lukewarm. Can you ensure it's served hot?
The serving sizes vary depending on who's serving; some staff give generous portions, others are very stingy.
The mess chairs are broken and wobbly, making it uncomfortable to sit and eat. Can they be repaired?
During the rainy season, the mess floor gets slippery and dirty, posing a safety hazard.
The coffee from the mess machine is always too weak or too bitter, never like proper coffee.
The biryani served on Fridays is usually just rice with a few pieces of meat and no flavor. It's disappointing.
There's no system for providing feedback anonymously; students fear retaliation if they complain openly.
The vegetables used are often of poor quality—bruised potatoes, limp spinach—that affect the taste.
The mess bill is deducted from our fees, but with such low quality, it feels like a waste of money.
The music played in the mess is too loud and not to everyone's taste. Can we have a quieter environment?
The food waste is high because many students don't eat the mess food due to poor quality. This is unsustainable.
The mess sometimes serves non-vegetarian food that smells foul, as if it's not fresh. This is especially concerning in the summer.
The juice served is often diluted with too much water, tasting more like flavored water than actual juice.
The tables are not wiped clean properly after each use, leaving food crumbs and stains that attract pests.
During early morning classes, breakfast is not ready on time, forcing us to skip meals or buy expensive snacks.
The mess does not accommodate students with dietary restrictions, like gluten-free or lactose-free options.
The food is so salty sometimes that I have to drink water constantly, and it's unhealthy for blood pressure.
The mess hall lacks proper ventilation, making it hot and stuffy during meals, which reduces appetite.
The snacks provided between meals are just biscuits or rusks, which are dry and uninteresting. Can we have fruits or yogurt?
The milk tea is either too sweet or not sweet at all, with no consistency in preparation.
The mess committee announced a new menu, but it hasn't been implemented even after a month. What's the delay?
I have two exams scheduled for the same slot on Friday: Chemistry at 9 AM and Physics at 9 AM. How am I supposed to be in two places at once?
My economics and history exams are back-to-back with only 15 minutes between them, and they're in buildings on opposite ends of campus. I won't even have time to catch my breath.
The exam timetable has my mathematics paper at 2 PM and my computer science practical at 2:30 PM on the same day. I need at least an hour for the practical, so this clash is impossible to manage.
I live in Gandhi Hostel Block B, and my exams are scheduled at 8 AM and 11 AM in different halls. With the shuttle bus being unreliable, I'm worried I'll be late for the second one.
Why are all my major exams crammed into three days? I have four papers with barely any gap for revision or rest.
My exam clashes with a mandatory lab session that contributes to continuous assessment. If I miss the lab, I lose marks, but skipping the exam isn't an option either.
I requested a reschedule for my sociology exam due to a medical appointment, but the new time now clashes with my political science paper. This is so frustrating.
The university didn't consider that some of us have part-time jobs. My evening exam clashes with my work shift, and I can't afford to lose either.
I'm an international student, and my exam timetable clashes with an important visa appointment at the embassy. I've provided documentation, but no one has responded.
My two exams are on the same day, but one is in the morning and the other in the afternoon. However, the fan in my hostel room isn't working, and I can't sleep properly to prepare.
The mess food has been giving me stomach issues, and with exams clashing, I don't have time to eat properly or recover. This is affecting my performance.
I have a project submission due on the same day as two exams. How can I possibly manage all three without any extension?
The exam schedule was released too late, and now I find that my travel plans for the break are ruined because my last exam clashes with my flight time.
My physics and chemistry exams are scheduled for periods 3 and 4 on Thursday, but the syllabus for both is massive, and I need more time between them to study effectively.
I'm in the sports team, and we have a championship match on the day of my exam. I've trained all year for this, but the university won't allow an alternate date.
The exam hall for my first paper is in the old building, and for the second, it's in the new campus. With traffic, it takes 30 minutes to get there, but the gap is only 20 minutes.
I have a doctor's note requiring extra time for exams, but the scheduled clashes mean I can't use that accommodation because the exams overlap.
My roommate has exams at different times, and the noise in the hostel is unbearable when I'm trying to study between my clashing exams.
The library is always crowded during exams, and with my timetable so tight, I can't find a quiet place to revise between papers.
I submitted a clash form weeks ago, but the exam office hasn't gotten back to me. Now the exams are next week, and I'm stuck in limbo.
My computer science theory and practical exams are on the same day, but the practical requires software that only runs in the lab, which is booked for another class during my slot.
I have to move out of my hostel on the day of my last exam, but the exam ends at 5 PM, and check-out is at noon. This is so poorly planned.
The bus service from my hostel to the exam center is infrequent, and with exams close together, I risk missing one if the bus is late.
I'm taking a minor in philosophy, and the exam clashes with my major in engineering. The coordinators from both departments are blaming each other.
My anxiety is through the roof because I have three exams in two days, and the first one is at 8 AM after an all-nighter due to the mess food making me sick.
The exam timetable doesn't account for students with disabilities. I use a wheelchair, and moving between distant venues with clashing times is nearly impossible.
I planned my study schedule based on the preliminary timetable, but the final version has completely different times, causing clashes I didn't anticipate.
My group presentation is scheduled for the same day as my individual exam, and both are worth 40% of the grade. I need to be in two places at once.
The Wi-Fi in my hostel block is down, and I can't access online resources to study for my clashing exams. This is adding to my stress.
I have a family wedding during the exam period, and I requested leave, but now my makeup exam clashes with another regular exam. It's a vicious cycle.
The air conditioning in the exam hall is broken, and with back-to-back exams in that room, I'm worried about sitting through hours in the heat.
My scholarship requires me to maintain a certain GPA, but with these exam clashes, I'm afraid my grades will suffer because I can't prepare properly.
I'm a resident of Nehru Hostel, and the water supply is erratic during exams. With clashing schedules, I don't have time to queue for water.
The syllabus for one of my clashing exams was updated last minute, and I haven't covered all the topics because I was focusing on the other subject.
I have a job interview scheduled months ago, and it clashes with an exam. The university says exams take precedence, but this interview is crucial for my career.
My music exam requires practical performance at a specific time, but the theory exam is at the same time. How can I showcase both skills?
The exam invigilators are strict about entry times, and with clashes, I might be marked absent if I arrive late from another exam.
I depend on public transport, and the last bus leaves before my evening exam ends. If I have another exam early next morning, I'll be stranded.
My laptop crashed, and I lost all my notes for one subject. With exams clashing, I don't have time to recover the data or rewrite notes.
The cafeteria is closed during exam days, and with no time between exams, I have to go hungry or rely on stale mess food.
I have a religious observance that requires me to be at a ceremony during an exam slot. I requested accommodation, but the alternate time clashes with another paper.
The power outages in my hostel are frequent during exams, and with clashing timetables, I can't charge my devices or study at night.
My sports scholarship requires me to attend training sessions, but they clash with exam revision times. I'm torn between maintaining my scholarship and passing exams.
The exam paper leak rumor has caused panic, and with clashes, I can't focus on preparing for either subject properly.
I have to care for a sick relative during exam week, and the clashing schedule means I can't be there for them and also attend all exams.
The university changed the exam venues last minute, and now two of my exams are in rooms that are too far apart for the time given.
I'm on medication that makes me drowsy, and with exams close together, I don't have time to rest and recover between papers.
My part-time job as a tutor requires me to conduct classes during exam times, and I can't find a substitute because everyone is busy with exams.
The exam timetable was published without consulting student representatives, and now we have widespread clashes that could have been avoided.
I have a flight booked for a study abroad program, but the exam clashes with the departure time. I've paid for the tickets, and now I might lose them.
The hostel curfew is during exam nights, but with clashing exams, I need to study late in the library, and the security won't let me in after hours.
My bicycle got stolen, and now I have to walk between exam venues. With clashes, the walking time eats into my break time.
The exam schedule forces me to choose between two important papers because they overlap. This isn't fair to students who have worked hard all semester.
I submitted a medical certificate for exam postponement, but the new date clashes with another exam. The administration is not responding to my emails.
The fan in my exam hall is so loud that it distracts me, and with back-to-back exams there, I can't concentrate on any paper.
I have a lab exam that requires specific equipment, but the slot clashes with a theory exam, and the lab is only available at that time.
My roommate is also facing exam clashes, and we both need the room to study at the same time, leading to conflicts.
The university policy says exams should have at least a day's gap, but here I have three in 24 hours. This is exhausting and unfair.
I rely on notes from a friend who has exams at different times, but with clashes, we can't meet to share materials.
The exam timetable doesn't consider students who live off-campus. I have to commute an hour, and with clashes, I'm spending more time traveling than studying.
Professor consistently shows up 20 minutes late for our 8 AM lectures, leaving us waiting in the hallway outside Block B every Monday and Wednesday.
During the last exam review, the instructor made dismissive comments about students who asked questions, saying we should have paid attention earlier, which was really discouraging.
I've noticed that certain students from specific hostels, like Mahatma Gandhi Hostel, always get higher grades on subjective assignments, even when their answers are similar to others.
The teacher uses class time to rant about personal politics instead of covering the syllabus, and we're falling behind for the midterms on October 15th.
In the chemistry lab, the professor yelled at a group for a minor spill, calling them incompetent in front of everyone, which was humiliating.
My emails regarding the upcoming project submission on November 5th have been ignored for over a week, and now I'm worried about missing the deadline.
During office hours in Room 304, the teacher often takes personal calls and ignores students waiting for help, which is very unprofessional.
The professor cancelled three classes in a row without any notice, and we only found out by showing up to an empty classroom during Period 3.
In the economics lecture, the instructor made inappropriate jokes about cultural stereotypes, making several students uncomfortable.
The teacher refuses to provide feedback on our drafts, saying it's not his job, but the syllabus clearly states that guidance will be given.
For the calculus final, the professor set questions from topics he never covered in class, which is unfair and has caused widespread panic.
The faculty member in charge of the programming course publicly mocked a student's code during a presentation, causing embarrassment.
I suspect grading bias because my friend and I submitted similar essays, but I got a C while he got an A, and the teacher won't explain why.
The teacher consistently interrupts students during presentations, especially female students, and doesn't let them finish their points.
During a group discussion, the professor singled out a student for their accent and made fun of their pronunciation, which is unacceptable.
The lecturer uses outdated materials and refuses to update them, even though the textbook has been revised and new editions are available.
In the history class, the teacher dismisses any viewpoints that contradict his own and penalizes students in grades for disagreeing.
The professor scheduled a mandatory review session at 7 PM on a Friday in the library basement, which conflicts with many students' part-time jobs.
The instructor shares confidential grade information with other students, violating our privacy and academic integrity.
During the physics practical, the teacher was more interested in his phone than supervising, and when an experiment went wrong, he blamed us instead of helping.
The teacher promised extra credit for attending a seminar but then denied it to everyone, saying he never made such an offer.
In the literature class, the professor reads from his notes without engaging with students, and when asked to clarify, he says it's all in the textbook.
The faculty advisor for our project group is never available, and we've missed two milestone submissions because he didn't sign off on our proposals.
The teacher uses derogatory language when referring to students from certain backgrounds, and it's creating a hostile learning environment.
During exam invigilation, the professor accused me of cheating without evidence and threatened to fail me on the spot, which was terrifying.
The lecturer consistently overruns class time by 15-20 minutes, making us late for our next classes in other buildings across campus.
The professor gave us a take-home assignment but then changed the due date at the last minute via a late-night email, causing confusion.
In the art studio, the teacher critiques work in a way that feels personal and damaging to students' confidence, rather than constructive.
The instructor cancelled the final project presentation without alternative assessment, and now our grades are based solely on one midterm exam.
The teacher plays favorites by allowing some students to re-submit assignments after the deadline while refusing others the same courtesy.
During a field trip, the professor left students behind at the museum and didn't account for everyone, showing negligence.
The lecturer uses class time to promote his own business ventures, which is irrelevant to the course and a waste of tuition money.
The teacher publicly posted grades on his office door without anonymizing them, so everyone can see who got what score.
In the computer science lab, the professor helps only the students he knows personally and ignores others struggling with the code.
The instructor gave a pop quiz on material we haven't covered yet and then used it to justify lowering our participation grades.
The professor frequently makes errors in lecture notes but refuses to correct them even when pointed out, leading to misinformation.
During a debate in political science class, the teacher shut down a student for expressing a conservative view, showing bias.
The teacher is often unprepared for lectures, spending the first 10 minutes figuring out what to teach, while we sit idle.
The faculty member assigned a group project but didn't provide clear roles, and when conflicts arose, he blamed us for not managing ourselves.
In the biology class, the professor shows graphic videos without warning, which is distressing and unrelated to the lesson.
The teacher schedules mandatory meetings during exam week, adding unnecessary stress when we should be studying.
The lecturer uses sarcasm excessively when students make mistakes, making them afraid to participate in class discussions.
The professor gave feedback on assignments that was vague and unhelpful, like 'do better' without specific points for improvement.
During a practical exam, the teacher was distracted and didn't notice when equipment malfunctioned, affecting our results unfairly.
The instructor changed the syllabus after the semester started, adding new requirements without adjusting the timeline.
The teacher humiliates students by calling them out for low scores in front of the whole class, which is demoralizing.
The professor requires us to buy his own textbook, which is overpriced and not available in the library, forcing unnecessary expenses.
In the language class, the teacher corrects pronunciation in a mocking tone, discouraging students from speaking up.
The faculty advisor missed three consecutive appointment slots I booked through the portal, wasting my time and delaying my research.
The teacher uses the class WhatsApp group to send irrelevant memes and jokes at odd hours, but doesn't respond to academic queries.
During a lab session, the professor allowed some groups to use advanced equipment while restricting others, creating an unfair advantage.
The lecturer gave a lecture while visibly intoxicated, slurring words and making incoherent points, which is completely unprofessional.
The teacher promised to write recommendation letters but then ghosted students after the semester ended, damaging our grad school applications.
In the statistics class, the professor solves problems incorrectly on the board and gets defensive when students correct him.
The instructor assigned a 50-page reading due the next day without considering that we have other classes and commitments.
The professor uses derogatory terms for students with learning disabilities, which is against university policy and morally wrong.
During a presentation, the teacher answered his phone and had a loud conversation, disrupting the student who was speaking.
The lecturer takes credit for student ideas in his research publications without acknowledgment, which is academic theft.
The teacher gave everyone in the class a failing grade on an assignment because he was dissatisfied with the overall performance, without individual evaluation.
In the engineering workshop, the professor ignored safety protocols and pressured students to rush, leading to a near accident.

The desks in Lecture Hall B are consistently covered in a layer of dust, making it difficult to take notes without getting my hands and materials dirty, especially during morning classes when the sunlight highlights all the grime.

I walked into my 9 AM calculus class and found trash from the previous evening's event still scattered across the floor—empty cups and wrappers everywhere. It's disrespectful to students trying to learn.
The floor in Room 205 of the Science Block is so sticky that my shoes make a pulling sound with every step. It's been like this for over a week, and it's utterly disgusting.

Could someone please address the overflowing trash can in the corner of the Economics seminar room? It's attracting flies, and the smell is starting to permeate the entire space during our two-hour lectures.

I am writing to formally report the unsanitary conditions in Classroom D. The whiteboards are streaked with permanent marker and old ink, and the erasers are so caked with chalk dust that they're useless.
The windows in the north-facing classrooms are so filthy that natural light is barely getting through. It's depressing and makes it hard to stay awake during afternoon sessions.
There's what looks like mold growing in the corner of Room 312 near the ceiling. As someone with allergies, I'm concerned about the air quality, especially with finals coming up next month.
Why are the chairs in the auditorium always left with crumbs and stains? It feels gross to sit down, and I often have to wipe the seat first with my hand, which isn't hygienic.

The ventilation grates in the engineering lab are clogged with dust and debris. Every time the fan kicks on, it blows particles everywhere, which can't be good for the sensitive equipment or our lungs.
During my last period class in Block C, the janitorial staff started mopping the hallway right outside, and the strong chemical smell wafted in, making several students cough and one feel nauseous.
I found a used tissue stuck under my desk in the philosophy seminar room. It's these little things that make the learning environment feel unclean and neglected.
The shared computer keyboards in the IT classroom are visibly grimy and sticky to the touch. In this day and age, basic hygiene like wiping down surfaces should be a priority.
There's a persistent, unpleasant odor in Lecture Theatre 1, like old damp carpets. It's distracting and makes it hard to concentrate during important review sessions before midterms.
The trash bins in the corridor outside the classrooms are never emptied on weekends, so by Monday morning, garbage is spilling out onto the floor. It creates a terrible first impression for the week.
I slipped on a wet patch in the hallway near Room 101 yesterday; there was no caution sign, and my notes got ruined. This is a safety hazard as much as a cleanliness issue.
The blinds in the history classroom are so dusty that when they're adjusted, a cloud of dust erupts into the air. I've started sneezing every time the professor opens them.
After the art club meets in Room 208, there are always paint splatters and clay remnants on the tables. It's not fair for the next class to have to clean up before they can start.
The ceiling tiles in the chemistry lecture hall have brown water stains, and one looks like it's sagging. It gives the impression that the building is poorly maintained.
During my 8 AM class in the Business School, I often see cockroaches scurrying along the baseboards. It's alarming and suggests a deeper pest control problem.
The hand sanitizer dispensers mounted outside the classrooms are always empty. What's the point of having them if they're never refilled?
The floor in the language lab is littered with pencil shavings and scraps of paper from previous sessions. It seems like no one bothers to sweep between classes.
The door handles to the main lecture theaters are visibly grimy and feel sticky. In flu season, this is a real health concern for everyone touching them.
There are always empty soda cans and food wrappers left in the cup holders of the stadium-seating lecture halls. It's lazy and creates a mess for others.
The carpet in the graduate seminar room has several large, dark stains that look old and set. It's unsightly and probably harboring bacteria.
